newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta ag minister calls for grain delay probe.
newsitem.headline: Alberta ag minister calls for grain delay probe.

text.p: Alberta Agriculture Minister Walter Paszkowski on Friday joined three other western Canadian provincial cabinet ministers in calling for a federal probe of grain rail shipment delays to Pacific ports.

"After 30 years of rising costs, system breakdowns and lost sales, it has become obvious that continued efforts by the federal government to tinker with the regulatory and institutional controls are futile," Paszkowski said in a statement.

Paszkowski, who was re-elected in Tuesday's provincial vote, was busy campaigning when other ministers called for the probe on that day. He first raised his concerns in a February 12 letter to Canada's agriculture minister.
Transport ministers of British Columbia, Saskatchewan and Manitoba Tuesday called for a federal inquiry into delayed grain shipments to Pacific ports.
Heavy snow, extreme cold and equipment failure led to delays in rail shipments to Pacific ports since early January.
The Canadian Wheat Board faces more than C$15 million in demurrage fines and has deferred sales.
Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale said Monday he spoke to the presidents of Canadian National Railway and CP Rail System about speeding up grain movement.
Canadian Transport Minister David Anderson said Wednesday he would consider a probe.
